messages.content: is i do not know if my cousin is home the same as i know my cousin is not home?
no. the first leaves the answer open. your cousin might be home or might not. the other says you know they are not home. not knowing an answer is different from knowing the answer is no.
can you make a small conversation using that difference?
is your cousin home? i do not know yet. then shall we say nobody is there? no, let us ask before choosing that.
now i call and my cousin answers from home. what can i say now?
you can say your cousin told you they are home. that is new information instead of the open question you had before.
what if i only hear their voice and they do not say where they are?
then hearing them answer does not by itself say they are home. your first example said they answered from home, but without that detail you would still need to ask.
write the question that asks place without choosing home first.
where are you right now?
now they say they are at the library. make a sentence that does not keep the old home idea as fact.
my cousin is at the library, from what they just told me.
why is that different from i think they might be there?

you now have an answer from your cousin in the story. i think they might be there would leave the place more open than the words they gave, although you can still make clear it is information from them.
answer simply.
you have an answer from your cousin now. it is different from only choosing a possible place yourself.
i came home after a long day at work and washed one cup. i had wanted to clean the whole kitchen, but the cup was all i did before sitting down.
you did one part and then stopped. do you want to talk about feeling tired, or would you rather just tell me about the evening?
i just want to tell you. the cup was the one i use for tea. i liked seeing it ready for tomorrow.
then that one small task had a clear place in your day. it made your tea cup ready, even if it did not make the whole kitchen clean.
keep the idea simple.
you came home after work, washed your tea cup, and sat down. you liked knowing the cup was ready for tomorrow.
i do not want to turn that into everyone should only wash one cup.
you do not have to. it is what you did that evening, not a rule for every kitchen or every person. the rest of the work can still be there without changing the fact that one cup is clean.
write a short note without making it sound like a large task.
i wanted to clean the kitchen, but after work i only washed my tea cup. then i sat down. i liked seeing it ready for tomorrow.
ask my last request simply.
write a short note about what happened without making it a large story.
now keep it two sentences.
after work, i washed my tea cup and then sat down instead of cleaning the whole kitchen. i liked knowing the cup was ready for tomorrow.
write a story about a child who thinks a radio is broken because there is no sound. an uncle asks one question before trying to fix anything.

a child sat near a radio and waited for music. when nothing happened, she told her uncle it was broken. he came over and asked whether she had turned it on. she looked at the radio, then said she had not. they turned it on together, and a voice came from it. the child had been right that there was no sound, but not right about the reason. her uncle asked if she wanted music or a story, and she chose music.
can the story keep her question as useful rather than make her feel wrong for asking?
yes. she heard no sound and asked for help. the question from her uncle helped find the reason. you can keep the story kind by making them try together instead of having anyone laugh at her.
say it simply.
she heard no sound and asked for help. her uncle asked a question, and they found out what to try together. the story does not need anyone to laugh at her.
write one calm line from the uncle.
let us check whether it is on before we try to fix it.
what changed when the radio was turned on?
there was sound, so the example no longer gave a reason to say the radio could not work. the first quiet was because it had not been turned on.
now give a short end with them listening.
they sat near the window with the radio on, listening to the music for a while.
i have one book with many pages. if i count six pages i read, does that mean i read six books?
no. pages are parts of one book in this example. reading six pages does not turn one book into six books.
answer simply.
no. you read six pages of one book, not six books.
now i read three pages from another book too. how many books did i read from?
you read from two books: six pages from the first and three pages from the other.
can you say i finished two books?
not from how many pages you read alone. you read parts of two books. you have not said how long each book is or that you read every page.
make that simple.
you read from two books, but you have not said you finished either one.
now i say the first book only had six pages, and i read all of them. keep the other book open.
then you finished the first book. you read three pages from the other book, but have not said whether that was all of it.
write that in my voice without adding a feeling about reading.
i finished the first book and read three pages from the other one.
my plan was to go to the library before lunch and visit my sister after lunch. now the library opens later, so i want to do both after lunch. i do not know the order yet.
then you can keep the library and the visit without choosing their order too soon. you need to know when the library is open and when your sister is free after lunch.
say it simply.
you still want the library and the visit. you need a time that works for each before choosing which comes first.
my sister is free at two. in this made up plan, the library opens at three.

then visiting your sister at two and going to the library after it opens at three could work, if there is enough time for the visit and the journey. the order is possible, but you still need that detail.
the visit can end at three, and the journey takes an hour. what time could i get to the library?
you could get to the library at four if you leave your sister at three and the journey takes one hour.
what if i say i will still be at the library at three?
that would not work with leaving the visit at three and taking an hour for the journey. you would need to change the visit time, the journey, or the hour you give for the library.
answer simply.
you cannot leave your sister at three and finish an hour journey at three too. in that plan, you get there at four.
now write the last order without saying any real library is open then.
in this made up plan, you visit your sister from two to three, then go to the library and get there at four.
ask my last request simply.
write the order in the made up plan without turning it into a fact about a real library.
my sister asked me how to write a question about our aunt visiting. i wrote would you like to visit tomorrow. does that mean i asked our aunt myself?
not just from writing an example for your sister. you helped with the words, but you have not said you sent them to your aunt as your own request.
keep the question simple.
i wrote words my sister could send to our aunt about a visit. does writing the example mean i asked our aunt myself?
now my sister sends the words and my aunt says yes. whose plan is it in this story?
your sister asked, and your aunt said yes to her. you helped with the writing, but have not said you are going too.
answer simply.
your sister and aunt have the visit plan. you helped write the words, but you have not said you are going too.
can i still ask if i can join them?
yes. you could ask: would it be okay if i came too? that is a new question, not something already chosen by writing the first message.
join is okay. now they say yes. what changed?
now they have said you can come as part of that visit. before, you only helped with the message.
say it simply.
now they have said you can come too. before that answer, writing the message had not made you part of the visit plan.
write a story about a person and their cousin hearing the same song. one can remember a meal with family, and the other can remember a long journey. do not make one memory more real than the other.

a person and their cousin heard a song while sitting in a room after lunch. one said it made her think of an old family meal, with people talking over the music. the other remembered hearing it during a journey, looking out of a window while everyone near him was quiet. they had been in different places, and the song had become part of both. for a while, each told one small detail. then they listened again without trying to make what they remembered the same.
make the story simple.
a person and their cousin heard the same song. one thought of a family meal, and the other thought of a journey. they each told a small detail, then listened together again.
what is a good question for one cousin to ask the other?
what part of that day do you remember when you hear this song?
can you make it less like there must be one clear answer?
what comes to mind when you hear this song, if anything?
now one says they only remember a color and the sky, not where they were. write a kind reply from the other.
you do not have to remember the whole place. you can tell me about the color and sky if you want.
what if i want the story to end without either giving more detail?
then let the song be the end of their talking for now. they can listen together and keep some parts of the memory to themselves.
now write that end simply.
they let the song play and sat quietly for a while, each with a different picture in mind.
picoboi, answer in two sentences. i want to tell a friend i read their message and will answer after work. do not say why work is busy.
i read your message. i will answer after work.
now make it one sentence, keeping both parts.
i read your message and will answer after work.
does will answer mean i have already answered?
no. it says what you plan to do later. reading the message has happened, but the answer is still to come in those words.
now i have answered after work. change only that time part.
i read your message and answered after work.
if i say i might answer after work instead, what changes?
might leaves it as possible rather than saying it is the plan you will follow. the time is still after work, but you have not said you will answer then for sure.
answer simply.
i might answer after work leaves open whether i will do it then.
keep it simple.
i might answer after work leaves open whether i will do it then.
